_comment: Accepted Semgrep findings (contrib/semgrep/README.md, 'Accepting a finding'). findings: fingerprint -> {rule, path, reason, by, date}. rule_paths: [{rule (glob), paths (globs), reason, by, date}]. Every entry needs a reason a reviewer can check.

rule_paths.reason: probe_host() sends an HTTPS HEAD to check that the depends/ download hosts are reachable before a devnet build; it reads no body and fetches no calibration input.
The same probe_host() HEAD request: its URLs are the fixed depends/ hosts in build.py, never a data input.

Every hit runs an argv list without a shell (git apply on a .work worktree, ybcal's own sub-runs, semgrep/git in the CI scanner, test fixtures); ybcal.subprocess.shell (critical) fails any shell use. Checked 2026-10-23. contrib/secops/code-scanning-triage.py (2026-10-24): gh api argv lists from constants and the workflow-supplied repository name, run only by the code-scanning workflow.
SHA-1 here keys an in-process model cache and labels a run with a short data fingerprint; nothing authenticates data with it. Input integrity is the sha256 in each provenance sidecar (data/fetch.py).

ybcal writes CSVs of numbers, timestamps and fixed column names for itself to read back (load_price_csv) and for reports; they are not a spreadsheet-import path, so formula injection does not apply. Checked 2026-10-23.
The module names come from in-repo constant tables (the CLI routes, STUDY_MODULES), never from input.
_picklable() only calls pickle.dumps to test whether a worker can go to a process pool; nothing is unpickled from a file. ybcal.data.unsafe-deserialization (critical) fails any pickle load.
